subject: GovCloud marketplace onboarding: procurement & PO path for CloudGov Solutions
messages:
From: Jill Smith <procurement@cloudgov.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood onboarding for AWS GovCloud listing / procurement questions

Hi Vanessa,

We're preparing to list Redwood on our GovCloud procurement catalog and would like to get vendor onboarding started. A couple quick items so we can scope procurement and legal:

- Do you have a GovCloud-compatible marketplace listing path (AWS GovCloud / Azure Gov / GCP regional restrictions)?
- What PO/invoice cadence do you accept for government customers (annual master PO vs. monthly invoices)?
- Required forms: seller intake, W9, SOC evidence? Any special FedRAMP or data handling notes for GovCloud?
- We'd prefer to execute an NDA before sharing sample SOW language; can you route one?

We're hoping to have vendor registration completed by the end of May. Attaching our internal supplier request (we will send formally if you need a vendor number).

Thanks — please loop your marketplace/contact ops and procurement owner.

Best,
Jill Smith
Procurement Lead
CloudGov Solutions

Attachments: CloudGov_Supplier_Request.xlsx (attachment referenced)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jill Smith <procurement@cloudgov.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace <mp-accounts@amazon.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding for AWS GovCloud listing / procurement questions

Hi Jill — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top and a proposed mutual action plan below.

Quick answers:
- Yes — we support listing in AWS GovCloud and can do Azure Government and GCP regional controls; there are a couple of extra paperwork items for GovCloud (KMS boundary and extra attestation in our seller intake).
- We can accept an annual master PO (preferred) or monthly invoices; annual is easier for reserved capacity pricing but we can accommodate monthly for pay-as-you-go pilots.
- Required: signed seller intake form, W9 (or W8 if applicable), signed NDA if you want one in place, and a brief SOC 2 pointer (we provide a redacted summary and auditor contact).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Today — exchange NDA and seller intake form (you complete intake and return).
2) 3 business days — Legal & Procurement review NDA and PO template; Redwood provides PO routing and invoicing contacts.
3) 1 week — Redwood submits marketplace listing artifacts to AWS (partner account, tax forms, support contact).
4) 2 weeks — Soft listing + test account; 3–4 weeks for live listing depending on marketplace backlog.

I've attached our Redwood_Seller_Intake_Form.pdf and a PO template (Redwood_PO_Template.docx). I'll loop in our internal procurement/partnerships team so we can align on billing, SLA and GovCloud KMS notes.

Next step: can you sign and return the attached NDA? If you prefer, we can DocuSign it.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_Seller_Intake_Form.pdf; Redwood_PO_Template.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood onboarding for AWS GovCloud listing / procurement questions — CloudGov (action items)

Team — forwarding the CloudGov request. Key asks: GovCloud listing, NDA, PO cadence (annual preferred by customer), and confirmation of required artifacts (SOC pointer, KMS boundary note).

Can you confirm:
- Ben: procurement routing & whether we can accept their annual master PO as-is or require our standard MSA?
- Karthik: marketplace listing owner — will Partnerships push the artifacts to AWS GovCloud? Any special controls for KMS?
- Marcus: finance contact for invoicing cadence and billing account setup; please confirm invoice email and tax onboarding steps.

I attached their supplier request. I'd like to circulate a clean MAP and send the NDA today.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood onboarding for AWS GovCloud listing / procurement questions — CloudGov (action items)

Thanks Vanessa. Quick notes:

- Annual master PO: we can accept an annual master PO. We'll need the PO number and an explicit billing address. For government customers, we route POs through our finance portal; I attached the PO routing instructions and a PO template (Redwood_PO_Template.docx).
- MSA: preferred but not strictly required for marketplace listings; if they include special terms or indemnities, legal should review.
- Invoicing cadence: finance supports both annual prepay(invoiced once) and monthly invoicing with Net30. For reserved capacity discounts tied to annual PO, we typically require the PO to reference the reserved capacity SKU.
- Legal contact for exceptions: legal-ops@redwoodinference.com (they handle NDA redlines for procurement).

I'll coordinate with Marcus on the invoice email and make sure the finance portal is ready to accept CloudGov's vendor number.

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template.docx (PO example); PO_Routing_Instructions.pdf

Cc: AWS Marketplace <mp-accounts@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding for AWS GovCloud listing / procurement questions

Hi Vanessa — attaching the signed NDA and initial PO per the MAP.

We completed the seller intake form (attached) and signed the NDA via DocuSign. A few clarifying questions before we route the PO formally:

1) KMS / key management: will Redwood require cross-account KMS keys in our GovCloud account, or do you hold the keys? We need an attestation on key ownership for the listing artifacts.
2) Data residency: for Gov workloads will Redwood guarantee that inference logs and KV caches remain in GovCloud-only buckets?
3) Billing reference: PO 000457 references a reserved pilot for 12 months; can you confirm the SKU and that reserved pricing will be applied once Redwood confirms receipt of the PO number?

1) KMS / key ownership: Redwood will use customer-owned KMS keys for GovCloud listings where required. Karthik has noted the KMS boundary requirement and will prepare an attestation template.
2) Data residency: we will ensure inference logs and ephemeral KV cache remain in GovCloud regions; Marcus will confirm storage buckets and access controls.
3) Billing / SKU: Ben confirms reserved-pilot SKU application once we receive the formal PO number. Ben — please confirm receipt and apply reserved pricing for PO 000457.

Operational items I've kicked off: Partnerships will create the GovCloud partner artifact package and submit to AWS MP (mp-accounts is CC'd). Legal-ops will hold the NDA (I've looped them). Finance (Marcus) will send a vendor onboarding link to Jill for invoicing and tax docs.
